key_insight: Collaborating AI agents derived and experimentally tested a minimum-calibration result for quantum spins in diamond, rejecting initially supportive but drift-compromised evidence.
engineering_relevance: Peer-checking agents and drift-aware validation could make automated quantum-hardware characterization more reliable.
method: Generate and critique research questions using collaborating language-model agents.
Derive minimum calibration settings for a defined microwave pulse family and check the result computationally.
Design discriminating experiments, monitor reference signals and revise protocols when evidence is inconclusive.
evidence_signal: Repeated reference measurements exposed drift in the initial experiment; a revised experiment met the unchanged acceptance criteria and supported the theoretical predictions.
watch_item: The demonstration concerns a defined pulse family in diamond spin ensembles; broader hardware applicability and robustness remain unestablished.
paper_title: Collaborative AI agents for autonomous experimental research with solid-state quantum spins
